Sasha (PM): Quick heads-up — need to rebalance the roadmap for the recommendation flow work: batching, prefix caching, quantization recommendations, and eval-triggered alerts. Three customer asks driving this: lower token cost, <100ms P95 for mobile, and fast detection of quality regressions. I sketched 3 lanes: Cost (batch + quant), Latency/Reliability (adaptive batching + routing), Quality (eval alerts + baselines). Need prioritization + minimal launch gates by EOW. Opinions?

Mike (Eng): +1 to lanes. Suggest we split batching into dynamic server-side batching (infra effort) and mobile-friendly batching (client heuristics). Dynamic gives biggest unit-cost wins but is riskier.

Linda (ML): For quantization, we need model profiles (fp16, int8, q4) + per-model quality baselines. Recommend starting with Llama2-family and the top 2 community models we support. Need an eval harness before any rollout.

Anna (Solutions): Customers want a simple knob: "cost vs latency" slider in Console + migration checklist. Also ask for example rollout docs for Dedicated customers (privacy/regulatory notes).

Tom (SRE): Important: aggressive batching can blow up P99. We need canary + per-route latency heatmaps, token-level cost breakdown in metrics, and circuit-breaker SLOs. Also define rollback triggers.

Sasha (PM): Draft minimal launch criteria so we can align: 1) Quant profiles and perf matrix for top-3 models; 2) Batching policy with SLO override and canary path; 3) Eval-triggered alerts prototype with sample policies and runbook; 4) Customer-facing "cost vs latency" knob with default presets. Anything missing?

Mike (Eng): Add measurable rollout metrics: cost delta (% tokens), latency P95/P99, and quality change (eval score delta). We should put explicit thresholds in the spec so engineering knows when to stop.

Linda (ML): For quality thresholds: propose relative thresholds to each customer's baseline (e.g., generation recall drop <2% or human-critical metric). BLEU-like metrics are brittle — prefer task-specific evals + periodic human spot-checks.

Anna (Solutions): Quick customer map: AcmeHealth = accuracy-first, RetailCo = cost-first (30% token reduction target), StartupX = latency/mobile-first. I'll build an impact matrix mapping lanes -> customer win conditions.

Tom (SRE): Operational checklist: canary routing at 5% -> 25% over 24h, automated rollback if eval-alert rate > X or P99 latency delta > Y. Also need a small chaos test for KV cache correctness.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot created epic RDW-1423 and linked PRD: https://redwood.internal/epics/RDW-1423 :rocket:

Sasha (PM): Next steps: Mike + Linda to draft technical spec (perf targets, benchmarks, quant knobs) by Tue EOD. Anna to own customer impact matrix. Tom to author SLO guardrails + rollout recipe. I'll collate and run a prioritization workshop Wed 10am. :calendar:

Mike (Eng): Noted. I'll slot an experiment: q4a quant + prefix caching on 10% traffic first.

Linda (ML): I'll start benchmark scripts and share a snippet in the repo. Example quickbench:```bash
# quant benchmark snippet
python bench.py --model llm-2 --quant q4 --seq 512 --batch 1 --iters 100
```

Anna (Solutions): I'll gather customer rep availability for Wed and attach their asks to the impact matrix.

Tom (SRE): I'll add observability dashboards (per-route token cost, P95/P99, eval-alert count) and a small runbook with automated rollback steps.

Sasha (PM): Perfect. If you hit blockers, ping me or drop brief notes here. We want a crisp set of gates (no more than 4) so sales/customer success can communicate a clear expectation. :+1:
